summary: Lands the Desk v2 stack tip (e0ad62ad, bot-06-quality-security/desk-v2-assembled-prompts) onto main as one draft PR. The tip was 17 ahead / 39 behind main because PRs #17-#24 were squash-merged into intermediate stack branches only. Rebased those 17 commits onto origin/main rather than merging, so each seat's commit and authorship survives and no already-merged stack parent is rewritten. Two add/add conflicts resolved by hand. One real regression found and fixed: main's #16 tightened G-4 and the tip's change document predated the new rule.

strategy.why: The 17 tip commits are linear and only 2 of them touch a file main also changed, so a rebase resolves conflicts twice rather than collapsing seven seats' work into one merge commit. Rebase replays the tip onto main; it does not rewrite the stack branches, which still point at the original commits.
strategy.rejected: A merge commit would have preserved the same content but buried the per-seat attribution that G-1 and G-2 read, and would have made the per-commit ownership replay below impossible.

Added both to the Layout block.

Kept main's version entirely and added only the tip's G-7 step. The tip's copy of this file was an OLDER snapshot of the template that predated main's #12-#15 hardening: it carried `--bot "${{ steps.bot.outputs.bot }}"` interpolated into run:, `RECEIPT=$(ls -1 ".receipts/${{ ... }}"/*.json | head -n1)`, an unanchored `^bot-0[0-6]-` regex, and no `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. security_findings_carried_forward.title: .github/workflows/gates.yml — branch/bot name interpolated into shell
security_findings_carried_forward.verdict: VALID against the tip. The tip's copy of the live workflow ran `--bot "${{ steps.bot.outputs.bot }}"` inside run:, and validated the bot id against an unanchored `^bot-0[0-6]-`, which accepts `bot-01-$(id)` and carries it into a later shell.
security_findings_carried_forward.disposition: FIXED on this branch. The acting bot is now derived from the GITHUB_HEAD_REF / GITHUB_REF environment variables rather than a ${{ }} expansion, validated against `^bot-0[0-6]-[a-z0-9-]+$` (anchored at both ends), and passed to later steps through an env: block as "$BOT". No ${{ }} appears inside any run: body in either gates.yml.
security_findings_carried_forward.how: The conflict resolution kept main's hardened body (#12-#15) and discarded the tip's older pre-hardening copy, adding only the tip's genuinely new G-7 step. Verified by grep: every ${{ }} in both .github/workflows/gates.yml and ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml sits in an env: block.

security_findings_carried_forward.title: gates.yml — receipt path shell injection
security_findings_carried_forward.verdict: VALID against the tip. The tip's copy ran `RECEIPT=$(ls -1 ".receipts/${{ steps.bot.outputs.bot }}"/*.json | head -n1)` and then interpolated `${{ steps.receipt.outputs.path }}` into three further run: bodies.
security_findings_carried_forward.disposition: FIXED on this branch. BOT, BASE_REF and RECEIPT all reach the shell through env: and are referenced as quoted variables. The receipt is additionally now selected from the diff (`git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d "origin/$BASE_REF...HEAD"`) rather than by globbing the directory, which also closes the stale-receipt fail-open main's #16 fixed.

security_findings_carried_forward.title: .github/workflows/desk-intake.yml, new from PR #22, audited for the same class
security_findings_carried_forward.verdict: CLEAN. It declares `permissions: {}`, passes attacker-controlled issue title, body and author login through env: rather than interpolating them, and builds its JSON with `jq -n --arg`, which cannot be escaped out of. `set -euo pipefail` is set.
security_findings_carried_forward.residual: The intake token is passed as `-H "Authorization: Bearer $DESK_INTAKE_TOKEN"` on the curl argv, which is readable from /proc on a shared runner. Negligible on an ephemeral GitHub-hosted runner and not a P1; left for INFRA rather than changed here, since it is outside what this landing needs to fix and would edit an INFRA-owned file.

This receipt was committed with `git add -f`: .gitignore ignores .receipts/**/*.json while every tracked receipt is committed, and both G-2 and the workflow require one. Same condition every previous receipt hit; unchanged here.

Trees were compared per-file against main, but the replayed commits' trees were not compared one by one against their originals — only the cumulative result was.
observations: PRs #17-#24 were squash-merged into intermediate stack branches rather than into main, which is how main came to lack services/desk-gateway, contracts/tool-rosters, grokbot/, infra/desk-gateway and skills/desk-bootstrap while all eight PRs read as merged. Worth a note in the stack procedure: a squash-merge into a branch that never reaches main leaves the PR green and the repository unchanged.

The tip carried an older copy of .github/workflows/gates.yml than main did, so a naive 'prefer the tip' resolution would have silently reverted the #12-#15 shell-injection hardening on the live workflow. main's gates-template-sync.yml is what makes that recoverable: because the live body must equal the template body, the correct resolution is mechanical rather than a judgement call.
G-4's surface-coverage rule from #16 will do this to every change document written before it. Any other stack branch still waiting to land should expect the same failure and the same one-line fix.
